retention.scope_note: All charts and analyses in Section 09 use only the 60 Wave 1 Fin Adopter participants. Wave 2 Non-Adopters are excluded because they have not yet deployed Fin and therefore cannot exhibit retention or post-deployment dissatisfaction signals.

methodology.test_fallback: Fisher's exact (when any expected cell count < 5)
methodology.intensity_collapse_rule: Per magnitude-coding-framework Section 5.7: kappa < 0.6, collapse to binary (high=2+3, low=1) for analysis. Intensity stacking not used in this report due to heavily skewed binary distribution.
methodology.segmentation_finding: Both wave-specific psychographic segmentations (W1 Adopters n=60; W2 Non-Adopters n=120) produced k=2 solutions with Jaccard stability below the 0.60 'do-not-publish' threshold (Hennig 2007). The 60 Adopters and 120 Non-Adopters are too homogeneous within their respective cohort identities to split into stable psychographic clusters at this sample size. Cohort splits in this report use the criterion variables (wave, replatform_likelihood_band, adoption_likelihood_band, likely_choice) and firmographic dimensions (platform, company_size_band) as direct categorical cuts, which are publishable directly.
